scope: Research question templates derived from R4 gaps. These are untested interpretations and MUST NOT be labeled validated or original discoveries.

hypotheses.title: PROX1: functional replacement must outlast an early retinal response
hypotheses.statement: If targeted extracellular PROX1 transfer inhibition engages a lasting regenerative program, then independently examined human-relevant retinal models should show mature, integrated new neurons, not only transient cell-state markers.
hypotheses.prediction: Reproducible lineage-resolved new retinal neurons with physiological connectivity and maintained function beyond the initial intervention window.
hypotheses.disconfirmation: Proliferation or neuron-like markers occur without genuine new functional connections, or improvements disappear on follow-up.
hypotheses.alternatives: Injury severity, surviving neurons, treatment localization, maturity of human tissue models.
hypotheses.evidenceNeeded: Replication in independent tissue models; direct identity and integration measures; long-term safety and persistence.
hypotheses.caution: A mouse mechanism and a human donor-tissue observation are not proof of clinical efficacy.

hypotheses.title: ASCL1: regenerative competence depends on injury-stage context
hypotheses.statement: If injury-stage regulatory context affects ASCL1-mediated retinal regeneration, then matched cell-state comparisons will reveal distinct injury-triggered accessibility or transcriptional responses in fish and adult mammalian Müller glia.
hypotheses.prediction: Reproducible species- and context-dependent state differences associated with documented retinal regeneration responses.
hypotheses.disconfirmation: Comparable injury responses and reprogramming competence after accounting for cell state, tissue age, and sampling methods.
hypotheses.alternatives: Fish paralog specialization, developmental stage, injury type, platform batch effects.
hypotheses.evidenceNeeded: Ortholog-aware expression comparisons, single-cell state trajectories, and appropriately matched functional outcomes.
hypotheses.caution: Zebrafish ascl1a necessity does not prove that ascl1b has the same role or that ASCL1 enables human repair.

hypotheses.title: Optic axon elongation is insufficient evidence of circuit repair
hypotheses.statement: If growth signaling alone fails to specify synaptic targets, then models with more regenerated optic-nerve axons will not necessarily show proportional restoration of target-specific circuits or vision.
hypotheses.prediction: A mismatch between anatomical axon length and independently verified synapse targeting, physiology, or vision-related function.
hypotheses.disconfirmation: Across replicated contexts, anatomical regrowth reliably predicts precise synaptic reconnection and recovered function without additional guidance.
hypotheses.alternatives: Assay sensitivity, circuit compensation, neuron survival, source of measured function.
hypotheses.evidenceNeeded: Independent anatomical and physiological endpoints; specificity controls; longer-term follow-up.
hypotheses.caution: PTEN is a tumor suppressor. This template does not advocate gene deletion or treatment.

hypotheses.title: Adult human retinal marker induction may not establish durable new neurons
hypotheses.statement: If short-term neural-lineage marker induction is an incomplete surrogate for retinal neuron regeneration, then replicate adult-donor culture results may diverge from measures of mature identity, synaptic integration, or durable activity.
hypotheses.prediction: Across independent donors, marker-positive cells lack one or more well-supported hallmarks of mature connected retinal neurons despite expression changes.
hypotheses.disconfirmation: Multiple independent donor studies show sustained mature cell identities, specific synapses and physiological integration aligned with the proposed lineage markers.
hypotheses.alternatives: Donor selection, culture injury, imaging ambiguity, classification of glia versus neuron-like cells.
hypotheses.evidenceNeeded: Independent replication, stronger lineage identification, blinded functional characterization, follow-up.
hypotheses.caution: The cited 2026 human donor tissue result is a preprint and is not clinical restored vision.

hypotheses.title: PRRX1 repair roles are conditional on cell lineage and tissue
hypotheses.statement: If PRRX1-family activity represents a context-dependent mesenchymal repair program, then some regulatory features may recur across zebrafish heart repair and axolotl limb blastema studies while downstream tissue outcomes remain distinct.
hypotheses.prediction: Replicable overlaps in lineage-resolved injury-response signatures with clearly distinct organ-specific targets.
hypotheses.disconfirmation: No shared response signature remains after accounting for lineage identity, stage and methods, or apparent overlap is limited to generic wound response.
hypotheses.alternatives: Paralog identity, mesenchymal subpopulations, tissue sampling, injury timing.
hypotheses.evidenceNeeded: Explicitly ortholog-aware comparative profiling and independent functional perturbation evidence for any proposed causal claim.
hypotheses.caution: Axolotl Prrx1 observation is not a demonstrated knockout requirement for limb regrowth.

hypotheses.title: Postnatal maturation constrains heart regeneration
hypotheses.statement: If postnatal maturation restricts cardiac muscle regeneration, then age-matched studies should reveal a decline in cardiomyocyte proliferative competence associated with the shrinking neonatal mouse repair window.
hypotheses.prediction: Age-dependent differences in lineage-verified cardiomyocyte replacement and functional repair that remain after accounting for injury model.
hypotheses.disconfirmation: The apparent age effect disappears after controlling injury method and outcome definitions, or direct regeneration is equivalent across tested ages.
hypotheses.alternatives: Injury method, neonatal resection variability, polyploidy versus division, fibrosis and survival.
hypotheses.evidenceNeeded: Lineage-specific cell-cycle evidence, injury and developmental-stage matching, independently measured function.
hypotheses.caution: Neonatal mouse repair and adult human cell turnover are not interchangeable endpoints.

hypotheses.title: YAP–EN1 scar outcomes depend on fibroblast context
hypotheses.statement: If fibroblast identity mediates regenerative effects of YAP–EN1 signaling, then scar architecture and restored skin appendages will vary with fibroblast lineage and timing rather than uniform YAP activity across tissues.
hypotheses.prediction: Independent tissue-level outcomes correlate with specific fibroblast state changes and retain wound integrity over time.
hypotheses.disconfirmation: No context-specific relationship replicates or observed scar changes come with worse healing or lost tissue function.
hypotheses.alternatives: Wound tension, fibroblast heterogeneity, epithelial interactions, tissue maturity.
hypotheses.evidenceNeeded: Independent model replication; tissue architecture; appendage function; long-term wound integrity.
hypotheses.caution: This is not a recommendation for generalized YAP inhibition or a proven scar-free human therapy.

hypotheses.title: Anti-Nogo-A efficacy, if any, may vary by prespecified injury class
hypotheses.statement: If clinical response to anti-Nogo-A differs by baseline injury class, then a future independently powered and prespecified analysis may reveal a reproducible interaction between baseline severity and the clinical effect.
hypotheses.prediction: A prospectively specified and replicated treatment-by-injury-class interaction on a validated functional endpoint.
hypotheses.disconfirmation: No replicated differential treatment effect, or exploratory subgroups fail prespecified confirmation.
hypotheses.alternatives: Subgroup multiplicity, timing, functional rehabilitation, baseline measurement and random imbalance.
hypotheses.evidenceNeeded: Prospective confirmatory evidence, predeclared analysis, overall primary outcome reporting.
hypotheses.caution: The cited NG101 phase 2b overall primary endpoint was not met. This hypothesis does not convert that trial into a success.

hypotheses.title: Nail-region anatomy constrains distal digit regrowth
hypotheses.statement: If retained nail-associated anatomical structures contribute to distal digit regeneration, then comparable distal injuries with different residual tissue anatomy should show distinguishable regrowth outcomes even after accounting for age.
hypotheses.prediction: Reproducible location-dependent anatomical associations supported by relevant cell-lineage or signaling evidence.
hypotheses.disconfirmation: No consistent anatomy-regrowth association after adjusting for injury severity, or differences fully explained by unrelated variables.
hypotheses.alternatives: Age, tissue retention, injury level, wound care setting and outcome reporting.
hypotheses.evidenceNeeded: Clearly documented injury location, anatomical endpoints and controlled observational interpretation.
hypotheses.caution: Historical human fingertip case reports do not establish whole-limb regrowth or self-care guidance.

hypotheses.title: Myostatin-driven size does not guarantee regenerated muscle function
hypotheses.statement: If myostatin-associated hypertrophy is partly distinct from tissue repair, then larger muscle size will not reliably predict restoration of injured muscle strength or physiological function across matched studies.
hypotheses.prediction: Repeated dissociation between mass/volume and measured post-injury motor performance or tissue integrity.
hypotheses.disconfirmation: Robust and reproducible concordance of structural repair and functional recovery matching changes in muscle mass.
hypotheses.alternatives: Genetic baseline, training, developmental compensation, fiber quality and injury type.
hypotheses.evidenceNeeded: Independent mass, strength, tissue-integrity and post-injury functional endpoints.
hypotheses.caution: A human inherited genetic case is not a controlled treatment trial or proof of injury regeneration.
